newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts up forecasts as Philips pleases.
newsitem.headline: Analysts up forecasts as Philips pleases.

text.p: Analysts broadly welcomed Philips' rise in first quarter profits on Wednesday, with many upgrading their earnings forecasts as recent restructurings began to pay off.
The benefits were particularly marked in consumer products, which turned in a better-than-expected operating profit of 206 million guilders ($107 million) after a year-earlier 52 million loss.
"This was very much better than expected...restructuring benefits are starting to come through," said Susan Anthony, a London-based analyst at Schroders.
She said operating income at consumer products was some 100 million guilders above her forecast, while semiconductors also did better than expected and financial items improved.

Frits de Vries, analyst at Theodoor Gilissen Bankiers, also cheered the figures: "These results are outstanding. I think we will see more improvements in consumer electronics in the rest of this year and also in the first half of 1998."

He said the cost savings currently achieved through the Sound & Vision restructuring should be sufficient to guarantee further improvements, adding that any additional measures would come on top of that.
De Vries said he would probably keep his profit estimates unchanged at 6.00 guilders per share for 1997 and 7.50 in 1998.
But Jan Balt of Effectenbank Stroeve said he would likely upgrade his 1997 earnings estimate to 6.00 guilders from his previous estimate of 5.00 guilders.
Balt said there were some signs of a recovery at minority-owned Grundig, adding he expected a further improvement of the ailing German affiliate and of the consumer electronics activities a whole.
"1998 could become a very good year for Philips...but earnings at Philips fluctuate enormously," he said.

NIB Securities analyst Rene Verhoef said he had been most impressed with the apparent turnaround in consumer products, adding he estimated the deconsolidation of Grundig to have had a positive effect of 80 to 90 million guilders on operating results at the division.
Philips said earlier this year it would no longer absorb all Grundig's losses in its own results, becoming a passive 32 percent shareholder.
Verhoef said he would upgrade his earnings forecast for 1997 to some 7.25-7.50 guilders from 6.50, and for 1998 to 8.50 or 9.00 guilders from a previous 7.50.
Schroders' Anthony said she would "definitely" upgrade her earnings per share estimates.
She said she would likely to raise her forecast of net normal income per share for 1997 to more than seven guilders from 6.45, and for 1998 to more than ten guilders from 9.50.
"But there is a danger of too high expectations," she said.

"All quarterly results will inevitably look good on a year to year comparison, but we have to look at the underlying performance....There were some points that performed somewhat worse than expected...Is there going to be another restructuring programme at some later stage?" she asked. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 ($ = 1.925 Dutch Guilders)
